facts.fact: 结局第一段（回家）：因为没有出租车，一家人分两趟回 Alba 的公寓——Juan 先带 Carlos 和孩子们（车里有披萨又有热气，孩子们 flushed 又困），午夜过后 Juan 再回 Splau 接三个还躺着聊天的女人；Alba 和 Diana 起身利索，替姿势僵久的 Carmen 扶起身来。进门看到的是没布置完的餐桌：银餐具全堆在中间，橄榄发暗；Carlos 坐在沙发上脸色苍白、精神不佳，见到她们只微微点头；婴儿在他脚边熟睡（回家路上又睡了一觉，还裹在婴儿座椅里）；其他孩子在一间卧室里玩，声音听起来平静、显然都很累。Diana 说「My God, I’ll have to throw out these clothes.」，Alba 说这身是全新的、Carmen 则教用小苏打加漂白剂走 prewash 漂掉血渍（但 Diana 说自家洗衣机和妈妈们的都有 prewash）；Carmen 自己脱下血淋淋的球鞋扔进厨房垃圾桶，Juan 要求三个女人都换掉血衣（「The kids can’t see you like this」），并说「maybe a shower would be good」；Alba 回「I’m not exhausted.」Juan 双手捧住妻子的脸仔细检查她血肉模糊的耳朵、难以置信地哼了一声，伸手要摸她头上有没有割伤或肿块时被 Alba 轻轻抓住手腕制止，Juan 没有追问也没有再说什么，只是走进走廊关上孩子卧室的门守在那里，直到 Diana 和 Carmen 换好衣服出来。
facts.anchor:
Since there were no taxis after all, they went to Alba’s apartment in two shifts. First Juan took Carlos and the kids. The pizza combined with the heat in the car had made them flushed and very tired. Then, sometime after midnight, Juan went back to Splau for the women, who were still lying down, chatting away. Alba and Diana got up easily enough, and the three of them helped Carmen stand. She’d gotten stiff after so much time in one posture. Now on their feet, they looked at one another.


“My God,” Diana said. “I’ll have to throw out these clothes.”


“Throw them out? No way. This outfit is brand-new.”


“Mom, you know bloodstains are impossible to get out. Just look at us.”


“You just sprinkle on a little baking soda, then some bleach, then throw it in on prewash. Or does your machine not have prewash?” Carmen said.


“My washing machine has prewash, Mom. It’s the same as yours and Alba’s.”


The first thing they saw when they walked through the door was the half-set table, all the silverware piled up in the middle, the olives looking dull. Carlos was sitting on the couch, appearing pale and out of sorts. He greeted them with a slight nod. The baby was fast asleep at his feet; he’d dozed off again on the way home and was still snuggled in his car seat. They could hear the other children playing in one of the bedrooms, their voices sounding peaceful enough, all of them surely very tired. Without taking off her coat, Carmen walked straight to her son-in-law.


“Why the long face? You’re always so serious! Cheer up, it’s Christmas Eve!”


“I don’t think it’s such an odd thing,” he said, “given the day we’ve had.” His voice was a thread.


“Carmen, before you sit down, would you mind changing out of those clothes?” Juan asked his mother-in-law as she removed her blood-soaked sneakers and threw them into the kitchen trash can. “All three of you should. The kids can’t see you like this. You can put all your clothes in the washer. I know you must be exhausted, but maybe a shower would be good.”


“I’m not exhausted,” Alba said.


Juan held his wife’s face in his hands and very carefully examined her flayed ears. He huffed in disbelief. When he started to feel her head for cuts or swelling, Alba stopped him, gently grabbing his wrist. Juan didn’t press or say anything else. He just went down the hall and closed the door to the kids’ bedroom, hovering there until Diana and Carmen passed.

facts.fact: Alba 独自走到阳台上，把 Switch 手柄从口袋里掏出来、用旁边的毛巾擦干净，塞进藏了大部分孩子礼物的大垃圾袋里（手柄被藏起来，孩子不知道）；站起来时眼前是熟悉的景色：城市灯光、深夜车流稀少的环城公路、足球场、巨型广告牌——广告牌已经换了，一个给 Finestrelles 商场、一个给 Splau，而她的公寓正好在正中间，离两个购物中心各两个出口；她笑了，回屋，并让 Carlos 保证别让孩子上阳台（那里有礼物）。
facts.anchor: Alba walked out onto the patio. She slid the Switch controllers out of her pocket, wiped them off with a towel lying nearby, and put them in the giant trash bag where she hid most of the kids’ gifts. When she stood up, she was face-to-face with the same view as always. The city lights, the ring road with minimal late-night traffic, the soccer field, the giant billboards. Alba leaned against the railing. She didn’t know when, but they’d changed the billboards. One was for the Finestrelles mall and the other for Splau. Her apartment was right in the middle, two exits away from each shopping center. Alba laughed and went back inside.

facts.fact: Juan 安排好所有人：三个女人进主卧室后他要求她们必须收拾干净才准出来，随后把孩子们叫到客厅看电视，理由是「Santa might pass them by」如果看到他们这么晚还在卧室玩；四个孩子抱着玩具鱼贯而出，Juan 一直盯着主卧的门确保它关着，然后说去车里拿没带上来的袋子（让 Carlos 看住，别拿进主卧）。孩子们爬上沙发、把靠垫扔到地上躺开，Juanito 抢到遥控器打开 YouTube 放自己最喜欢的 shorts，一个接一个全校都在传的歌和视频，六七个之后 Juanito 笑得嚎叫、Brigitte 在屏幕前 twerking，Carlos 尴尬地看着地面（他分不清是因为侄甥太早熟，还是看着自己的一对儿女一个假装会唱没听过的歌、一个抓着家具模仿表姐而心酸）；Tomás 要求「Put on the baby one」，屏幕上放的是一支瓶装水广告（两个成年人逛街时在橱窗里看到自己变成婴儿的倒影，跟着《Here Comes the Hotstepper》跳舞，婴儿做出小孩做不到的动作），表兄妹跟着比划，连 Carlos 也看呆了。Carmen 穿着睡袍和 Alba 那件偏小的抓绒袍、头发湿着往后梳，看起来精神不错，孩子扑上去抱她；Carlos 问她感觉如何，她答「Fine, fine」并说饿了、可以吃火腿奶酪或做点别的，可惜今年没做烤乳猪（suckling pig）；Carlos 说自己「I’m OK. I’m not hungry—I feel a little off.」
facts.anchor:
Juanito grabbed the remote and turned on the TV. He navigated to YouTube and showed his sister and cousins his favorite shorts. Every so often, one would make a request, a song or a video that, for some inexplicable reason, had swept through all the schools at once. At first, they calmly watched one after another. Six or seven videos later, Juanito was howling with laughter, and Brigitte was twerking in front of the screen. Carlos looked at the ground, oddly embarrassed. He wasn’t sure if the cause was his niece and nephew, so precocious, or the pathos of watching his own children, one pretending to know a song he’d never heard, the other holding on to the furniture in an effort to imitate her cousin.


“Put on the baby one,” Tomás said.


“Which baby one?”


“The one with the dancing babies, the one you like.”


Carlos again looked away from the sixty-five-inch screen, thinking that number seemed too small, that it had to be more like seventy-five. He heard the video begin playing—it was a classic in Alba’s home. They put it on all the time. The whole family loved it. Every time Diana’s family came over, they’d sit through at least three viewings.

facts.fact: Diana 借 Alba 的衣服穿：姐妹俩刚洗完头发、穿着几乎一样的毛衣加牛仔裤（Diana 的裤子略紧，但曾让她焦虑的事此刻已不重要）；脸却不像——Diana 像 Carmen、Alba 像她们的父亲，一个棱角分明一个圆脸，即使相差六岁凑在一起仍像双胞胎、几乎一模一样。Carlos 觉得嫂子哪里不对，最后发现是她把马尾放下来了：Alba 从来都扎低马尾、两缕头发垂在脸侧，今晚她散着头发是为了不让孩子看见她的耳朵；她用纱布和胶带尽力处理了伤口，还吃了止痛药（她一向极端排斥吃药），但还是疼；她知道自己明天——圣诞节——得去急诊，而要解释身上这些伤将是一场难题。
facts.anchor: The sisters had wet hair, too, and they were dressed almost identically, in sweaters and jeans. Diana was borrowing Alba’s clothes, and the pants were slightly tight on her, but at that point, what would have once been a major stressor seemed unimportant. Their faces looked nothing alike. Diana had Carmen’s face, and Alba had their father’s. One with angular features, the other, round. Still, when they were together, even with six years between them, they mimicked each other and somehow seemed like twins. Dressed similarly, with their faces freshly washed, they were practically one and the same. But Carlos thought something was off about his sister-in-law; he couldn’t figure out what it was. In the end, he realized she’d undone her ponytail, and he had always seen her with her hair pulled back. A low ponytail, two strands framing her face. Tonight, Alba had left her hair loose so the kids wouldn’t see her ears. She had done her best to treat them by patching them up with gauze and tape, and she had even taken a painkiller—rare for her, since she avoided medication at all costs. But it hurt. She knew she’d have to go to urgent care tomorrow—Christmas—and that explaining all her injuries would be a challenge.

facts.fact: Diana 和 Alba 几分钟内就收拾出平安夜晚餐：收走玻璃杯和银餐具、卷起塑料桌布、连纸盘上干掉的剩菜一起扔进垃圾桶，桌子折起一半，端上甜食、坚果和虾；没人问谁要喝什么，她们自己从冰箱拿出香槟并取来杯子（Carmen 说「I’ll have a little」时朝 Carlos 使眼色，Alba 和 Diana 都怕开瓶，异口同声说等 Juan 来）。Juan 正好进门，开香槟时软木塞弹到天花板，孩子们又兴奋起来跑来围观，睡过 Juanito 整场 DJ 秀的婴儿也醒了、蹒跚跟在后面；Juan 像行家一样倒满五杯、每杯一样多再传开，他觉得还在哺乳期的 Alba 要喝香槟有点怪但没说，只为她想喝而高兴。他和 Carlos 举起杯子沉默碰杯，两人都说不清为什么举杯、也都不敢看对方的眼睛。母子三人手挽手在沙发上喝了整三瓶香槟、就着虾看 65 寸电视上的圣诞特别节目，Carmen 不断夸主持人和歌手的衣服、笑圣诞节目总是这么老派；Carlos 和 Juan 觉得该不该劝她们少喝点，但谁也不敢说；孩子们回卧室玩，每隔几分钟就出来吃零食或问圣诞老人什么时候来。
facts.anchor: Hand in hand on the couch, mother and daughters drank three bottles of champagne while eating shrimp and watching a televised Christmas gala on the sixty-five-inch TV. “Doesn’t it look amazing?” Carmen said to Diana every so often. They remarked on the outfits the hosts and musicians were wearing, and they laughed about how stuffy Christmas specials always were. After a while, Carlos and Juan thought that maybe the women shouldn’t be drinking so much, but they didn’t dare say a word. Sitting over by the table, they appeared to be watching TV as well, but in reality, they were trying—unsuccessfully—to process what had happened that night. Juan would refill the women’s glasses when they asked. And the kids had gone back to the bedroom to play, though they came out every few minutes for snacks, or to ask when Santa would show up.

facts.fact: 本章最关键的新信息由 Carmen 抛出：当年在营地帮她把章鱼控制住的是营地里的女人们。Alba 问「Mom, how did you keep the octopus from getting out?」，Diana 看着母亲和姐姐还不明白发生了什么、但知道自己身在其中——她肚子上有同样的疤，几小时前她差点被劈成两半，且知道自己迟早会弄明白。Carmen 说「The girls at the campsite helped me, way back then」，并点明是「Camp La Tortuga Ligera」；帮助她的是「The bingo lady and her friends. The women who played bingo at her camper.」——即 Diana 那位朋友 Manuel 的妈妈和她的朋友们；Diana 抢话「I knew they were doing weird stuff! Were they witches?」Carmen 说不只是帮她，那年夏天至少还帮了另外三个女人；她们有办法看出谁需要帮助，会主动过去问你怎么了并帮你；她们认为最好是把章鱼放出来，但会听你的理由，你若不想放，她们就告诉你怎么收回去、或者已经出来一半时怎么除掉；只要你不会陷入危险，你决定什么她们都帮忙，帮的事远不止这一件。Diana 讥讽她们是「scaffolding experts」，Carmen 笑着捂住嘴。
facts.anchor:
Then Alba asked: “Mom, how did you keep the octopus from getting out?” Diana looked between her mom and her sister. She still didn’t understand, but it didn’t really matter. She knew she was a part of it, part of the mystery, because she had the same scar on her belly, and because just a few hours prior, she had nearly been split in two. And she knew that in due time, she would figure it out.


“The girls at the campsite helped me, way back then.”


“What are you talking about?” Alba said.


“Camp La Tortuga Ligera, what else? What other campsite did we ever go to?”


“But who helped you?”


“The bingo lady and her friends. The women who played bingo at her camper.”


“My friend Manuel’s mom?”


“Yes, her. And her friends.”


“I knew it, Mom!” Diana broke in. “I knew they were doing weird stuff! Were they witches? Oh my God. Why didn’t you say anything before!”


Now it was Alba who was confused, but instead of asking questions, she tried to steer the topic back in her favor.


“But why did they help you? You weren’t very close with them, were you?”


“Not very close, no. But they helped. Not just me—a lot of the women there. At least three others that summer alone.”


“Why?”


“Oh, I don’t know. They wanted to. And they could. They had a way of seeing when someone needed help. They’d just go over to you, and ask you about it, and help you.”


“Insane,” Diana said. She couldn’t stop shaking her head.


“And they said you shouldn’t let it out?” Alba asked.


“What?”


“The octopus.”


“No, no, of course not. They thought it was best to let them out, but they’d listen to your reasons, and if you said you didn’t want that, they’d tell you how to contain them—or if they were already partway out, how to get rid of them. Whatever you decided, they would help you. As long as it didn’t put you in danger. They did a lot for the women there. It wasn’t only that.”


“They were scaffolding experts,” Diana quipped.


“That’s one example, yes,” Carmen said, covering her mouth to quiet her laughter.

facts.fact: Carmen 讲自己当年的经历：整个夏天肚子都不对劲，一直胀着，像怀 Alba 时那样有东西在踢、在动；有天早上（就是她在海滩中暑的那天）有东西从她肚脐里钻了出来——两个邻居把她拖回木屋时 Alba 吓得要命；她当时在沙上感觉无比平静，把手臂浸到水里弄湿脖子才整个人下水，随后腹部开始剧痛，一波一波像宫缩；她低头看见皮肤下有个小拳头形状的轮廓往外顶，然后顶破了——「Why do you think my belly button’s so ugly?」里面伸出一条小尾巴，左右摆动，血顺腿流下，水里也有血，「It was horrific, absolutely horrific.」Alba 当场纠正：那不是尾巴，是触手，她有两条，从肚子里出来；「Tentacles! Shiny tentacles.」「They looked like they were covered in glitter!」——还会在体内活动、跳舞，里面有光；Alba 笑得停不下来，坚持说这就是在 Splau 发生的（glitter tentacles at Splau），Diana 听得目瞪口呆；Alba 的笑传染给 Diana 和 Carmen，三人几秒内笑到崩溃：Carmen 笑出了眼泪，Diana 拍着沙发手心、几乎流口水、把香槟滴在沙发上，电视声音开得太大，Juan 和 Carlos 什么都没听见，只目瞪口呆地看着。
facts.anchor:
All that summer, something strange was happening with my stomach. I felt bloated all the time. It was like when I was pregnant with you—something was kicking, moving around. But one morning, something came out of my belly button. It was the day I got sunstroke at the beach. You were so scared when you saw the two neighbors dragging me back to the cabin. I felt so peaceful on the sand, and I dipped my arms in and wet my neck before going all the way into the water, and then I felt an awful pain in my stomach. It wasn’t constant, it came in waves, like contractions. Then I noticed something pressing against my abdomen. I looked down and saw a tiny fist pressing out from inside, just the outline under my swimsuit. It hurt like crazy. Imagine something pushing out from inside you. That’s what it did—it broke through. Why do you think my belly button’s so ugly? There was a tail coming out from inside me, a little tail that wagged back and forth. And blood was streaming out, down my legs, there was blood in the water, too. It was horrific, absolutely horrific.”


“It was a tentacle, Mom,” said Alba. “I had two.”


“Excuse me?” Diana said. “You had a tail coming out of your belly button, and you had an octopus tentacle? I’m not following.”


“No, not one—I had two.”


“You had two tentacles?”


“Yes, coming out of my belly.”


“What do you mean ‘tentacles’?”


“Tentacles! Shiny tentacles.”


“Shiny tentacles?”


“They looked like they were covered in glitter!” Alba started to laugh.

facts.fact: 结尾：Carmen 让 Alexa 放 'I Dream of You' by Camela（她把歌名记错了），Alba 纠正说歌名是 'Tears of Love'；前奏一响三人全都站起来跟着哼，Carmen 先唱那句「I don’t feel her beside me now, can’t hold her or touch her now」，Alba 惊讶「Mom, you know the words!」（Carmen：「How could I not! You drilled it into me!」Diana：「You played it all summer, Alba. Maybe two summers!」），副歌到来时三人互相搂住肩膀高声唱和：'I dream of you—what have you given me? Without your love, I would never have believed... I long for you, you’re forgetting me.' 孩子们听见动静跑出来，穿着 Primark 浴袍、头发还是湿的、脸没化妆，围着女人们又唱又跳、齐声唱副歌；Carlos 和 Juan 看呆了——没人见过这些孩子玩得这么开心、这么满足，尤其不在平安夜。全章最后一个动作是 Carmen 喊「Diana!」，Diana 问「What?」，Carmen 说「Why don’t you get an air fryer like the one your sister has?」——一句家常话收束全书。
facts.anchor:
Alexa, play ‘Tears of Love’ by Camela,” Alba said.


The first chords sounded, and all three got on their feet, humming along.


Carmen sang, “ ‘I don’t feel her beside me now, can’t hold her or touch her now. She’s not here anymore, she’s not here anymore.’ ”


“Mom, you know the words!” Alba exclaimed.


“How could I not! You drilled it into me!”


“You played it all summer, Alba,” Diana said. “Maybe two summers!”


“Alexa, louder!” Carmen commanded.


The chorus came, and they wrapped their arms around one another and started shouting the words: “ ‘I dream of you—what have you given me? Without your love, I would never have believed. I dream of you—what have you given me? I long for you, you’re forgetting me.’ ”


Hearing the commotion, the kids ran out, dancing and jumping in circles around the women. In their Primark robes, hair still damp, faces bare, they sang the chorus in unison, still with their arms around one another. Carlos and Juan couldn’t look away. The kids were ecstatic. No one had ever seen them have that much fun together. No one had seen them that happy—that content, especially not on Christmas Eve.


“Diana!” Carmen yelled.


“What?”


“Why don’t you get an air fryer like the one your sister has?”
